Shadowheart can be romanced. The following sections explain Shadowheart's romance-specific storyline.

Storyline

“
Another moment won't kill them, I suppose... Well, it might, but let's take that risk.
„
— Shadowheart, answering the romancing player character's request for a few more moments on their first night together

Act One

Tiefling party

At the tiefling party, if the player character has 20 or more approval with Shadowheart and has either not started any romance or is involved in no more than one other active romance, she invites them to "share a bottle" with her.

If the player character accepts, the rendezvous occurs later that night near a secluded waterfall away from camp. The conversation deepens their connection, and several dialogue options and skill checks follow. Exploring these fully reveals more of Shadowheart’s personality. Most choices do not affect approval, unless the player character abruptly ends the encounter. After the conversation, the scene fades and returns to a few hours later, showing the two lying on the ground, holding hands.

If the player chooses to stay with her through the night and succeeds a passive  DC 5 Insight Check, they realize she is expecting a kiss and can choose dialogue which leads to one. Failing the check does not lock the player out of her romance. Regardless of the outcome, the pair returns to camp together before dawn.

The next day, the player character can speak with Shadowheart about the previous night. Her response varies depending on her approval level and on what did or did not occur during the encounter. If the player character failed the Insight check, she may express disappointment, admitting she was almost certain a kiss was coming. However, saying they wish they had kissed her allows the relationship to continue. Responding positively about their time together progresses the romance, while saying it was a mistake or that they got carried away ends it.

Another way to connect

Alternatively, if Shadowheart’s approval reaches 40 or higher, a new dialogue option becomes available: "I can't help but feel like you and I might have missed a chance to connect. Truly connect." Choosing this unlocks a long rest scene in which Shadowheart invites the player character to spend time together: "It seems to be the perfect night to spend a little time together, just you and I... assuming you haven't changed your mind, of course?" If the player character agrees, the aforementioned waterfall scene follows, allowing to start Shadowheart's romance.

However, the "chance to connect line" option is no longer available once any of the following apply:

  • The player character is already dating or partnered with someone else.
  • The tiefling party already took place.
  • The party has left Act Two.

Grymforge

In Grymforge, the player character can find an  Idol of Shar. Giving it to Shadowheart grants approval and a special dialogue with her.

Selûnite player character

If romanced by a Selûnite cleric, unique conversation options are available with Shadowheart. For example, if the Idol of Shar is given to her by a Selûnite cleric, a unique romance dialogue option can be chosen: "Kiss me like you hate me." One of her possible responses to this challenge includes teasing the player character with the promise of a kiss as she slowly circles them from behind, kissing them a few times on their backside, before finally sharing a passionate kiss face-to-face.

Act Two

“
The gods fight over her, but is she truly that special?
„
— Sceleritas Fel, as he tasks a romanced Dark Urge with an unspeakable act of betrayal

In the Shadow-Cursed Lands, the player character can find a  Night Orchid. Giving it to Shadowheart grants approval.

The Gauntlet of Shar is an important inflection point and possible divergence in Shadowheart's romance. There, she must decide how to deal with the  Nightsong.

If Shadowheart accompanies the player character to the Shadowfell, she decides the Nightsong's fate and speaks with the player character immediately afterward, reflecting on what just happened and, if romanced and upon departing from the Shadowfell, on the nature of their relationship. This conversation can advance the romance to the Partnered stage or end the relationship, depending on the player character's response to her and on how she dealt with the Nightsong.

  • If she spares the Nightsong, she defies  Shar's will and is abandoned by her goddess. She then admits in the conversation after leaving the Shadowfell that her relationship with the player character is something that she has consciously ignored in favor of her faith, and asks if they want to make that relationship more serious. She confesses her desire to be with the player "now and always," and asks if they feel the same.
  • If she kills the Nightsong, she fulfills Shar's will and becomes a Dark Justiciar of her goddess. She then explains in the conversation after leaving the Shadowfell that she must fully devote herself to Shar, "leaving no room for others." However, she remains in a relationship with the player character if they insist they still want to be with her.

Act Three

Selûnite

If the player character previously learned that Shadowheart cannot swim and has 40 or more approval with her, she invites them to go swimming alone with her.

This scene has two versions, depending if nudity is turned on or not in the accessibility settings.

If nudity is turned off, both Shadowheart and the player character meet at a beach, where Shadowheart asks the player character to get into the water. After a playful swim, the scene cuts to the pair on the beach again, fully clothed, where they start kissing.

If nudity is turned on, Shadowheart asks the player character to strip and gleefully appraises them while they do. Both of them then walk into the water and enjoy a swim before returning to the beach, still naked, where they start to have sex.

After completing Shadowheart's personal quest at the House of Grief, Shadowheart asks the player character to come with her to a  Selûnite statue. Her dialogue there depends on how she dealt with her parents.

  • If she chose to kill her parents, she grieves their loss.
  • If she rescued them, she sobs that she does not deserve to be anyone's daughter for the actions she committed in Shar's name, only for her parents to reassure her that they love her and she will always be their daughter.

Either outcome gives the player character the option to comfort her with a hug.

Some time later, she talks about the future she hopes to have after getting rid of the Absolute. She talks about her desire to live in a rural cottage with a colorful garden and surrounded by animals, with the player character by her side.

Sharran

If Shadowheart kills the  Nightsong, she becomes imbued with  Shar's power and becomes noticeably colder and more distant. She informs the player character that Shar is her priority, but says her body is still at their disposal.

After completing Shadowheart's personal quest at the House of Grief, if she chooses to kill her parents, Shadowheart later invites the player character to a Selûnite shrine. She reveals she saved the blood that splattered on her clothing, body and hair from killing the Nightsong. Using it to desecrate the shrine, she relishes in the act.

If Shadowheart chooses to spare her parents the same statue scene as the Selûnite path plays with slight variations in dialogue. There is no additional romance scene.

Quotes

“
I'm sorry. I have a lot on my mind... the Shadowfell, Nightsong... I can think of little else.
„
— Shadowheart, apologizing after snapping at the player character's asking how she feels
“
With good reason. It is no coincidence that a daughter of the Moonmaiden spoke to you of wolves.
„
— Selûnite cleric player character, affirming Shadowheart's unmoored state
“
That's not the first time you've made such a leap. Maybe I shouldn't be entirely shocked – I did fall for a Selûnite after all.
„
— Shadowheart, replying to a romanced player character
